decisions.statement: RollbackPlan is multi-object, never a boolean
decisions.support: Independent derivation from vendor docs (Vercel omits env/config; Fly omits fly.toml/secrets/migrations) and operated local practice (donor standard: data rollback is separate; plus a third surface-route object)
decisions.falsifier: A rehearsed multi-object rollback leaves an object unrestored, or a single-object rollback proves sufficient across representative compositions

decisions.statement: Each rollback object carries its own recovery horizon; the minimum governs
decisions.support: PlanetScale schema revert bounded ~30min dual-write vs unbounded artifact rollback
decisions.falsifier: A composition recovered after its shortest horizon expired

decisions.statement: Pin by content digest and own artifact retention
decisions.support: Render re-pulls by tag and may get a different image; Fly may prune images not recently deployed
decisions.falsifier: A pinned digest proves unresolvable at rollback time despite owned retention

decisions.statement: Five runtime profiles derived from packaging mode
decisions.support: Reuse shapes already decided; sidecar is the only profile where a third party owns migrations
decisions.falsifier: A representative capability fits none of the five
decisions.note_wave2: S1-L4 contributes tiered per-action isolation selection (isolate/gVisor/microVM) as an open extension to the five profiles

decisions.statement: Minimum instrumentation contract belongs in HostContract
decisions.support: Requirements intersection across Grafana OTel attributes, Datadog Unified Service Tagging, Elastic traceparent, Harness SII, incident.io routing attribute
decisions.falsifier: Attribution achieved at dependency level without one of the five items

decisions.statement: Capability identity must be deliberately plural
decisions.support: New Relic warns multi-entity reporting causes duplicate groups and recommends consolidation — the opposite of what a composed app needs
decisions.falsifier: Per-capability attribution achieved under a single consolidated entity

decisions.statement: App-level release correlation is actively misleading for independently-deployed capabilities
decisions.support: Rollbar suspect deploy is the last deploy before first occurrence — a temporal heuristic; Sentry release health scores a whole release
decisions.falsifier: Temporal heuristics attribute correctly under independent capability deploys

decisions.statement: Instrumentability is a capability admission criterion
decisions.support: An uninstrumentable capability caps system attribution at the call boundary; failure is silent
decisions.falsifier: A capability that cannot be instrumented is nonetheless attributable in production

decisions.statement: ComputeSDK cannot be the load-bearing sandbox abstraction; it cannot express memory-preserving pause
decisions.support: Wave-2 source read: universal-sandbox.ts declares no pause/resume/suspend and its status enum ('running'|'stopped'|'error') cannot represent a paused sandbox; the E2B provider never passes keepMemory so the memory path is unreachable; a provider author's own comment calls getInstance() an escape hatch to the stateful API 'that ComputeSDK's core surface does not model'
decisions.falsifier: ComputeSDK's core interface gains pause/resume with a paused state, or memory-preserving pause proves unnecessary for warm previews
decisions.limitations: static read of the interface at main on 2026-08-27; no execution against a live provider

decisions.statement: Workflow acceptance gates above build gate
decisions.support: Local donor standard's required-proof list is workflow-shaped and operated; P14 known that a passing build is not workflow proof
decisions.falsifier: Acceptance suites prove too brittle or slow to run per release

decisions.statement: Do not quote Northflank one-click rollback; Statsig has no automatic rollback
decisions.support: First-party docs describe only re-triggering a prior run; Statsig docs describe alerting only
decisions.falsifier: First-party documentation of a dedicated rollback control

decisions.support: Account-wide quota killed wave-1; wave-2 recovered observability and rebuilt OSS
decisions.falsifier: A completed continuation wave closes it

decisions.statement: K long-lived schema versions is an extension of validated prior art, not a configuration option
decisions.support: Verified from project docs: pgroll and reshape each hold exactly two versions live, and that window is transient by design (exists only between start and complete; completing drops the old version and rollback becomes impossible). pgroll propagates writes to 'its counterpart', singular. Actionist needs K versions long-lived across independently-upgrading clients — a gap in both count and duration.
decisions.falsifier: A tool or technique sustains K>2 long-lived concurrent schema versions, or lockstep client upgrades prove acceptable
decisions.limitations: documentation read, not benchmarked at scale
